Testing yourself is not the end of studying: it is the fastest way to learn. Climb this ladder in order and log every result in [My progress](progreso.en.qmd).

<ol class="b-steps">
<li class="b-step"><strong>Check (after each module)</strong><p>Answer the module's self-assessment and its exercises <em>without looking</em>. With 80 % or more, move to the next topic.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>Timed practice (from week 2)</strong><p>Exercises by topic with a target time and the <a href="simulador/index.html">code lab</a>: 12 min per SQL query, 15 min per Python problem.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>Mock exams per part (weeks 3, 6 and 7)</strong><p>30-minute reasoning, 40 technical questions in 50 minutes and the 5-query SQL challenge in 60 minutes.</p></li>
<li class="b-step"><strong>Dress rehearsal (week 8)</strong><p>Reasoning 30 min + technical 90 min <em>back to back</em>, phone away, like December 18.</p></li>
</ol>

## Goals for December 15

| Test | Goal | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SQL | ≥ 30/35 without looking | Candidates report hard SQL, ~12 min per question and no margin for error |
| Python | 25/25 | They are short exercises: you should not miss any on exam day |
| Algorithms | ≥ 17/20 | Big O and pseudocode tracing appear as multiple choice |
| Reasoning | ≥ 24/30 in 30 min | Described as "quite demanding" |
| Technical (simulator) | ≥ 34/40 | 85 % leaves room for exam-day nerves |

## After every mock exam

1. **Log** the score in [My progress](progreso.en.qmd#mock-exam-log): the chart shows whether you are improving.
2. **Classify each mistake** by its cause and write it in the [mistake notebook](progreso.en.qmd#mistake-notebook).
3. **Attack the most frequent cause**, not the longest topic:

| Cause | What to do |
|---|---|
| Didn't know the concept | Go back to that point of the theory and redo the missed exercises within 2 days |
| Didn't understand the English | [How to read questions](english/como-leer-preguntas.en.qmd) + flashcards with the words you didn't know |
| Ran out of time | Timed blocks; in the exam, skip the hard question and come back at the end |
| Careless | Underline the word that changes everything (NOT, EXCEPT, LEAST, MOST) and check once |
| Fell for a trap | Write it as a rule in the notebook; for AIF-C01, review the confusable pairs (Spanish section) |

## Exam-day strategy

- **Fast first pass:** answer what you know and flag the doubtful ones. Come back at the end.
- **Time budget:** reasoning ≈ 1 min per question; technical ≈ 1 min per multiple-choice question and 12–15 min per coding problem.
- **Never leave a multiple-choice question blank**, unless the recruiter confirms that wrong answers cost points ([questions for the recruiter](guides/que-evalua-blend360.en.qmd#5-questions-worth-asking-the-recruiter)).
- **SQL:** before writing, look at the expected result: one row per what? That tells you the `GROUP BY`.
- The last 48 hours: the [final review](cheatsheets/repaso-final-48h.en.qmd).
